## Observed Facts

- **Team ownership cannot be determined from these logs.** The BGL dataset exposes only `alert_tag`, `component`, `level`, and `node` as columns [E2]. No team, owner, or service-catalog field exists, so I did not map any Component to a Team.
- Data Scope for the counts below: Dataset BGL, full time range 2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04, level FATAL, all nodes and alert tags [E1, E2].
- FATAL Log Entries by Component:
  - KERNEL: 626,450 [E1]
  - APP: 228,536 [E1]
  - LINKCARD: 206 [E1]
  - MMCS: 3 [E1]
- Total FATAL Log Entries: 855,195 [E1], out of 4,747,963 BGL Log Entries in the corpus [E2].
- KERNEL and APP account for almost all FATAL Log Entries (854,986 of 855,195) [E1]. These are Log Entries, not incidents.

## Hypotheses

- KERNEL and APP are the Components that most likely need Team ownership review first, because they hold nearly all FATAL volume. This is based only on the counts above, not on any ownership data.
- The FATAL volume in KERNEL and APP may be concentrated in a few nodes or alert tags. I have not checked this yet.

## Unknowns

- Which Team owns KERNEL, APP, LINKCARD, or MMCS. The logs do not contain this, so it has to come from your org's service catalog or on-call roster.
- Whether the FATAL counts are recurring or come from a few spikes. I have not run a trend.

## Next Step

Send me the Component-to-Team mapping from your ownership source, and I will join it to these counts. Before that, I can run `count_by` on KERNEL and APP grouped by `alert_tag` or `node` to show which sub-areas drive the FATAL volume, so the owning Teams have something specific to act on.
